title: Nepal Police raise toll to 547, injured count rises to 1,473
body: Nepal Police raised the confirmed toll to 547 dead in a Friday evening bulletin, ABC News reports, coming within minutes of Nepal's disaster authority, NDRRMA, putting the figure at 538. Nepal Police also reported 1,473 people injured in Nepal, up from 466 the day before. China's state media separately raised the Tibet side toll to 5, from 3. The flood hit Timure in Rasuwa on Wednesday morning and ran down the Bhote Koshi into the Trishuli and the Narayani.

Rescue counts vary by agency and by day. Police said 1,545 people caught in the flood had been rescued as of the 7am bulletin, and NDRRMA told ABC News on Friday afternoon that 3,253 people have now been rescued by helicopter across the flood zone, a still broader tally that has not been named or broken down. NDRRMA's own earlier, named list stands at 113. The Nepali Army said on Friday its helicopters had rescued 706 people from Timure, Syabrubesi and Mailung by 3pm, up from 449 at 12:20pm, including 40 foreign nationals: 29 Indian, 4 German, 4 Chinese, 1 Omani and 2 South Korean, Onlinekhabar reports. Nepal Tourism Board said 117 stranded tourists have now been rescued from the Bhotekoshi area, 85 of them Indian, 16 Chinese, 9 South Korean, 2 American and 2 Italian, with 3 not yet identified by nationality, Onlinekhabar reports. Twenty eight police personnel remain out of contact.

Friday's midday bulletin restated a fuller district breakdown, adding up to the earlier 489 total: Chitwan 186, Nawalparasi East 112, Gorkha 44, Dhading 40, Nuwakot 37, Tanahun 29, Nawalparasi West 28 and Rasuwa 13, Nepal Police said. No bulletin has yet broken the new 547 total down by district. Health facilities in Chitwan, which has the most bodies, can hold only around 50 at a time, which is slowing identification and release to families.

NDRRMA repeated its missing count of 977 people in Nepal in Friday afternoon's update alongside the new death toll, ABC News reports, so the figure has not moved since Friday morning. Nepal's tourism board says 517 of the missing are foreign nationals, from 33 countries. Out of contact does not mean dead. Phone lines, power and internet are down across the valley and are coming back slowly.

The barrier lake upstream near the Chhochen Khola and Purepu Tsangpo was reported to have breached, but Nepal's government has not confirmed a dam collapse and the two accounts have not been reconciled. Chinese state media report the lake has since grown rather than drained. See the update above for what is and is not confirmed. USGS first read the shaking on Wednesday as an earthquake, then found no earthquake took place: the signal came from an ice and rock avalanche that fell into the Lhende Khola on the Tibet side, dammed the river, then broke.

The Home Administration says 13,295 security personnel are working the flood zone: 7,250 from Nepal Police, 4,200 from the Nepali Army and 1,845 from the Armed Police Force, Khabarhub reports. Prime Minister Balendra Shah travelled to Bidur in Nuwakot on Thursday to see the damage.

In India, the NDRF and the Sashastra Seema Bal have rescue teams on standby in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, and the NDRF says the Gandak, which the Narayani becomes downstream, could see higher water levels. Nepal has turned down offers of search and rescue teams from India, China, the US, Britain, Japan, South Korea, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh, the Kathmandu Post reports. The government says its own army and police can handle the operation and is asking instead for cash, through a single channel into the Prime Minister's Disaster Relief Fund.
Keep off the banks of the Bhote Koshi, the Trishuli and the Narayani until officials say it is clear.
